items.title: Improvement: Enable QNX build and test for Rust unit-test targets
items.body:
### What

As part of #794, manual was removed from these Rust tests. They only build and run on Linux, so they carry target_compatible_with = ["@platforms//os:linux"]:

```
//score/mw/com/impl/rust/com-api/com-api-runtime-lola:com-api-runtime-lola-tests
//score/mw/com/rust/score_com_concept:score_com_concept-test
```
They are plain rust_test targets, with no QNX build or test path like the one `rust_unit_test` provides.

The Tokio integration test //score/mw/com/example/com-api-example:com-api-example-tokio-integration-test stays manual. Without the tag, the QNX build fails because socket2 0.6.5 can't resolve libc::TCP_KEEPIDLE. It also has sanitizer findings, which are out of scope here.

Goal

Make these Rust tests build and run for QNX, and remove the Linux-only constraint.

Acceptance criteria

bazel build/test --config=ci --config=qnx -- //score/... passes with the Linux constraint removed from the two tests.
The Tokio socket2 QNX build failure is resolved.

items.title: Improvement: `paste` crate usage in the Rust COM API
items.body:
### What

The COM interface macros use the paste! procedural macro to concatenate identifiers during compilation. This generates names such as interface, consumer, and producer types, along with accessor names such as getters and setters. The crate supports macro-based API generation; it does not provide runtime COM behavior.

Acceptance criteria

items.title: Improvement: `futures` crate usage in the Rust COM API
items.body:
### What

The Rust COM API uses futures for asynchronous stream and notification support. The public Subscription::to_stream() API returns a futures::Stream; the LoLa runtime uses futures::task::AtomicWaker to notify pending receives when samples arrive. The mock runtime also uses stream helpers and an executor in its support code.

This is used in API/runtime behavior, unlike a build-only procedural macro dependency. The COM API does not require application users to adopt a particular executor.

Acceptance criteria

- Record the pinned crate version, enabled features, and direct COM API call sites.
- Distinguish production runtime use from mock/test-only use.
- Review crate provenance, license, maintenance status, and safety relevance.
- Document whether to retain futures, reduce its use, or replace specific functionality, and record the required qualification artifacts.

items.title: Improvement: Provide an async stream of newly available services
items.body:
### What

The Rust API currently discovers services through` find_service::<I>()` which creates a discovery handle scoped to an interface and a `FindServiceSpecifier` Its async query returns an initial result, it does not continuously report services offered afterward.

Add an asynchronous stream that reports newly available services across the system, rather than only additional instances matching one service instance specifier. Since services may belong to different interfaces, stream items should provide interface-independent service descriptors, including enough information to identify each service.

**Acceptance criteria:**

The stream reports newly available services system-wide, not only later instances for one specifier.
Each item identifies its service and interface.
The API documents initial results, errors, and stream lifetime/termination.
Existing interface-scoped discovery APIs remain available.

Reference - https://github.com/eclipse-score/communication/issues/9

items.title: Improvement: E2E protection for Rust Method/Field APIs
items.body:
## What
Add E2E (End-to-End) protection for Rust `Method<T>`/`Field<T>` APIs (and, by extension, `Event`). Split out of #782 at @bharatGoswami8's request: https://github.com/eclipse-score/communication/issues/782#issuecomment-5580666403 — out of #782's milestone-1 scope, and no tracking issue existed for it.

## How
Not designed yet. Per the linked comment, E2E protection hasn't been considered so far even for the existing Rust Event implementation, so this needs a design discussion (aligning with whatever E2E mechanism exists on the C++ side, if any) before implementation.

## Estimates for realization
TBD, pending the design discussion above.

items.title: Improvement: Usage and Integration of External Crates in COM-API (e.g., paste crate)
items.body:
### What

The COM-API currently utilizes the external paste crate for declarative macros to simplify interface definitions. In future development, additional external crates may also be required.
Since these crates are not certified, we need to define a clear approach for how such dependencies should be handled within the score.

### How

Two possible approaches:

1. Integrate changes into the SCORE repository 

- Bring the relevant functionality or macro logic directly into the SCORE repo and maintain it internally.

2. Manual implementation

- Recreate the required macro or helper functionality manually within our codebase.
